Index.skinny_story_tagline: Brewed by hand. Born out of frustration. Built for freedom.
Index.story_intro: The revolution didn’t start in a lab – it started at the bar. In a smoky California bar in the 90s, a group of women asked for something unheard of: A drink without sugar. Without bloat. With less consequences.
Index.story_origin:
The bartender mixed vodka, soda and lime.
 “The Skinny Bitch,” they joked.
Index.story_alek_intro: Years later in Norway, Alek – a war veteran, paramedic, and fitness and health nerd – was staring at a wall of unhealthy drinks: sugar bombs in disguise, with labels full of lies.
Index.story_brewing: So he did what rebels do. He brewed his own.
Index.story_by_hand: By hand. In his kitchen. Can by can.
Index.story_on_no_sugar:
A drink with no sugar, no junk. Just clean, natural
ingredients – and a taste people came back for. The
goal wasn’t to drink more – it was to drink smarter.
Index.story_naming:
He called it Skinny Bitch. And the world judged hard.
 People were offended. Outraged. Loud.
Index.story_truth:
But here’s the truth they never saw:
 It was never about looks.
 It was about better choices.
Index.story_evolution:
The hate got louder – but the love got stronger.
 So we dropped the name they couldn’t handle.
Index.story_regret:
And kept what mattered:
 The rebellion. The recipe. The right to enjoy.
Index.story_tagline:
For the ones who dance all night and train at dawn.
For the ones who want joy without compromise.
For the ones who live loud and live light.

BBS.research_shows_paragraph: What you choose to drink matters more than you think. Most people see alcohol as the main problem. But it's often what comes with it — sugar, calories, overload  — that does the real damage.
BBS.alcohol_paragraph: Alcohol puts extra stress on your organs and can trigger inflammation. That means your body has to work harder to repair itself, impacting everything from metabolism to immune response.
BBS.sugar_paragraph:
large amounts of sugar — like what’s found in most ready-to-drink cocktails — and you get a combination your body struggles to handle.
Excess sugar is quickly converted into fat by the liver
BBS.sugar_paired: Paired with alcohol, the metabolic load becomes even greater.
BBS.calories_paragraph: One typical RTD cocktail can contain as many calories as a full meal. This hidden load adds up — leading to weight gain and disrupting your body’s balance over time.
BBS.need_paragraph: More people than ever are looking to make smarter choices — not just in what they eat and how they move, but also in how they drink. People still want fun. They still want to enjoy life. But they want to do it in a way that feels better — for their lifestyle and their values.
BBS.whySkinnysubTitle: No filters. No compromises. No apologies.
BBS.whySkinnyDescription: We created Skinny Cans to make it easier to choose smarter when you want a drink.
BBS.enjoyWithoutCompromise: So you can still enjoy — without compromise.
BBS.backing-1: A population-based cohort study found that regular consumption of sugar-sweetened alcoholic drinks is linked to significantly higher liver fat than alcohol alone.
BBS.backing-2: Consumption of Alcoholic and Sugar-Sweetened Beverages is Associated with Liver Fat Accumulation
BBS.backing-3: Excessive intake of dietary sugars induces chronic low-grade inflammation
BBS.bbs_header: Sugar and alcohol together put significantly more strain on the liver than alcohol alone. At the same time, high sugar intake triggers inflammation — worsening the total metabolic impact.
